description: Narrowly-bounded pivot: can a regularized partial-information rank aggregator safely combine a strong BM25 initial ranking with sparse cached LLM pairwise judgments? Reuses the same frozen SciDocs q50/k15 exhaustive gpt-4o-mini pairwise oracle as offline_active_acquisition_pilot_v1. No live provider calls, no new judgments, no qrel leakage into aggregation decisions.
frozen_schedule_selection_rationale: Chosen on the 15-query dev split, before any test-set inspection. Schedule shape: linear_decay had 0/15 severe-harm queries at 10% budget (vs inverse_coverage's 1/15) and tied-lowest at 5% (2/15, same as pseudo_count_cutoff, vs inverse_coverage's 3/15); its mean nDCG gain over BM25 at 10% (+0.065) was close to the other two (+0.067 to +0.074). Tie-broken toward linear_decay for interpretability: it reaches exactly lambda=0 at full coverage, unlike inverse_coverage which never fully releases the prior. lambda0 magnitude: 3 values tried (2.0, 8.0, 20.0) on dev at 5%/10% -- lambda0=2.0 had higher mean gain but markedly worse safety (4/15 and 1/15 severe-harm); lambda0=8.0 and 20.0 tied on safety (2/15 and 0/15) but 8.0 had higher mean gain, so 8.0 was frozen. See REPORT.md Phase 4 for the full recorded dev comparison, including all variants not selected.
correction: Holm, family = the 5 pre-registered primary comparisons above, evaluated only on the 35-query held-out test split
leakage_controls: regularized_aggregation.py functions take only (candidates, revealed-so-far outcomes, qrels-free BM25 prior, coverage-derived lambda) -- no qrels, no oracle object, no unrevealed outcome, no exhaustive ranking
the strongest-baseline selection for the AUC comparison uses only the 15-query dev split's AUC values, never the 35-query test split
the regularization schedule (shape + lambda0) is frozen from the dev split before any test-set metric is computed
